components.role: Normalizing flows are used as expressive generative models or differentiable density estimators to learn probability distributions, latent spaces, or dependencies between edges.
Density estimation provides the modeling framework to infer probability densities, likelihoods, or conditional distributions from observed data or feature spaces.
Uncertainty quantification evaluates epistemic and predictive uncertainty, capturing dispersion or posterior distributions over model parameters and structures.

target_task.text: The combination targets probabilistic modeling and structured inference tasks such as Bayesian causal discovery, reduced-order model closure, multiscale dynamics, and shape modeling.

limitation.text: Existing approaches often fail to capture complex dependencies, lack principled ways to incorporate expressive posterior learning, or do not adequately represent interactions and uncertainties in multiscale and structural systems.

combination.text: Normalizing flows are integrated into density estimation and probabilistic frameworks to model complex probability distributions and support uncertainty quantification over latent spaces, parameters, and structural dependencies.
